locationLabs.label: Manager lab
locationLabs.prompt: Review the current reservation confirmation process at check-in. Map every step from guest arrival through seating. Identify where confirmation gaps or handoff failures could occur. Then review the food-runner check-in/check-out process and dry-storage signoff controls.
locationLabs.deliverable: A one-page process map showing the reservation confirmation flow and shift accountability checkpoints. Identify two specific gaps and propose a concrete fix for each.

locationLabs.label: Manager lab
locationLabs.prompt: Examine a current menu item preparation standard. Walk through the method from raw ingredient to plated dish. Identify where the method could produce inconsistent results. Then review the Friday/Saturday reverse happy hour concept and how it creates a guest pathway from Tell Your Friends.
locationLabs.deliverable: A revised preparation standard for one menu item with specific method adjustments. A brief outline of how the cross-concept guest journey could be measured and improved.

locationLabs.label: Manager lab
locationLabs.focus: Handoff to Americano and event follow-through
locationLabs.prompt: Map the current guest experience at Tell Your Friends on a Friday or Saturday night. Identify the moment where a guest could transition to The Americano and what currently happens at that moment. Review event follow-through processes: what happens after an event is booked, confirmed, executed, and closed.
locationLabs.deliverable: A guest-journey map for a Friday night showing the Americano handoff point. A checklist for event follow-through from booking through post-event review.

locationLabs.label: Opportunity exercise
locationLabs.focus: Repeatable opening/closing standards and local guest feedback
locationLabs.prompt: Design a repeatable opening checklist and closing checklist for Neon Spur. The checklists should cover equipment readiness, station setup, cleanliness verification, and cash/POS procedures. Then design a simple guest feedback mechanism that captures actionable information without requiring technology the location does not have.
locationLabs.deliverable: An opening checklist and a closing checklist, each with specific verification steps. A guest feedback capture method with a plan for weekly review of collected feedback.

locationLabs.label: Manager lab
locationLabs.focus: Menu-transition consistency and manager log adoption
locationLabs.prompt: Review the current state of manager log usage at Bungalow Kitchen. Identify whether logs are being written consistently, whether they contain actionable information, and whether incoming managers read them. Then examine one aspect of the recent menu transition and assess whether service standards have stabilized.
locationLabs.deliverable: An assessment of manager log adoption with specific recommendations for improving consistency. A stabilization report on one menu-transition element with evidence of whether the standard is being met.

locationLabs.label: Opportunity exercise
locationLabs.focus: Opening-readiness discipline and source-of-truth launch checklist
locationLabs.prompt: Build a source-of-truth launch checklist for a new restaurant opening. The checklist should cover staffing readiness, menu finalization, equipment verification, vendor setup, training completion, and operating system setup. Each item should have a clear owner and a verification method. This is a planning exercise, not a timeline commitment.
locationLabs.deliverable: A launch-readiness checklist with categories, specific items, assigned ownership, and verification criteria. The checklist should be usable as an ongoing status tracker during the opening process.

tools.title: 7-Day System Reset
tools.content:
7-Day System Reset

Use this when operating discipline has drifted. Pick one week. Recommit to the fundamentals.

Day 1-2: Audit

  • Are manager logs being written daily?
  • Is inventory being counted on schedule?
  • Are shift handoffs happening?
  • Is the weekly variance conversation scheduled?

Day 3-4: Correct

  • Restart any lapsed system with a brief re-training
  • Write the standard on one page and post it
  • Verify completion for two consecutive shifts

Day 5-7: Sustain

  • Check that each system ran without prompting
  • Recognize the team member who executed best
  • Schedule the next reset check for 30 days out

The goal is not perfection. The goal is restarting the rhythm.

tools.title: Manager Problem-Solving Brief
tools.content:
Manager Problem-Solving Brief

Use this format when presenting a problem to leadership. Arrive with the problem, the cause, and your proposed fix.

Problem

What happened? State the specific issue in one sentence. _____

Cause

Why did it happen? Identify the root cause, not the symptom. _____

Impact

What was the operational impact? Be specific. _____

Proposed Fix

What is your recommended corrective action? _____

Verification

How will you confirm the fix is working? When will you check? _____

The discipline is presenting with a solution, not just surfacing problems.
